The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9b1b750b309e5c5a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 9-10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: There are smooth connected projective varieties X∗, X′, W, Z, a birational morphism X′ → X∗, and morphisms X′ x − → W g − → Y, h : W → Z, q = h ◦ x, with the following properties. (i) The variety X∗ is a smooth model of X carrying a resolved absolute Iitaka map for KX + DX. Its boundary D∗, and the boundary D′ on X′, follow the strict-transform-plus- reduced-exceptional convention. The map q is the pullback of this Iitaka map, and (2.4) dim Z = κ̄(U). (ii) The morphisms x, g, h are surjective and have connected fibers and geometrically integral generic fibers. The induced map from W to its image in Y × Z is generically finite. In particular, Wz → g(Wz) is generically finite for very general z. (iii) The divisor D0 W = (g∗DY )red is SNC. On very general fibers over Z, all the relevant varieties and boundary strata are smooth, and (2.5) κ X∗,z, KX∗,z + D∗|X∗,z  = κ X′ z, KX′ z + D′ |X′ z  = 0. 10 OPENAI One may make further compatible smooth birational modifications, retaining these assertions. After the finite preparations in this section, X∗ can be fixed as an earlier model, and every subsequent source model is taken to dominate it.
